--- title: "The Hierarchy of Algebraic Structures and Spaces" subtitle: "From Magmas and Semigroups to Monoids, Groups, Rings, Fields, Modules, Vector Spaces, Lattices, Categories and Monads — and the Parallel Ascent from Sets to Topological, Metric, Normed, Hilbert, Measure, and Probability Spaces" author: "Igor Kan" date: "2026-09-14" categories: [Mathematics, Abstract Algebra, Topology, Category Theory, Analysis] description: "A comprehensive map of the structures of mathematics: the algebraic ladder from magma and semigroup through monoid, group, abelian group, ring, integral domain, UFD, PID, Euclidean domain and field to modules, vector spaces and algebras; the order-theoretic ladder to lattices, Boolean and Heyting algebras; the category-theoretic world of functors, natural transformations, monads and adjunctions; the spatial ladder from sets to topological, metric, normed, inner-product, Hilbert, Banach, measure and probability spaces; the hybrid structures (topological groups, Lie groups, topological vector spaces, C*-algebras); a giant Mermaid flowchart connecting them all; axiom-dropping counterexamples; and a Python laboratory that verifies the axioms of finite groups, fields, vector spaces, lattices, Boolean algebras, small categories, and the list monad." format: html: html-math-method: mathjax code-fold: show code-tools: true toc: true toc-depth: 4 number-sections: true jupyter: python3 toc: true toc-depth: 4 number-sections: true --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} *"Mathematics is the study of structures, and mathematical structures form a hierarchy ordered by the axioms they satisfy."* — **A structuralist motto** Every branch of mathematics studies **sets equipped with structure**. Add a binary operation, get a magma; add associativity, a semigroup; add an identity, a monoid; add inverses, a group; add a second operation, a ring; add inverses to the second operation, a field. In parallel, add "closeness," get a topology; add a distance, a metric space; add a norm, a normed space; add an inner product, a Hilbert space. This essay draws the **complete map**, with a single all-encompassing flowchart, and verifies the axioms computationally. ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ### Companion Treatises in this Series - [Probability Theory and Mathematical Probability](probability-theory-and-mathematical-probability.qmd) - [Sequences, Series, and Convergence Tests](sequences-series-and-convergence-tests.qmd) - [Axiomatic Set Theory, ZFC, Ordinals, Cardinals, and Paradoxes](axiomatic-set-theory-zfc-ordinals-cardinals-and-paradoxes.qmd) - [The Rational Line: Density, Enumeration, Cauchy Sequences, Dedekind Cuts, Metric Spaces, and Topology](rationals-density-enumeration-metric-spaces-and-topology.qmd) ::: --- ## 1. Structures as Signatures Plus Axioms ::: {#def-structure} #### Definition 1.1 (Mathematical structure) A **structure** is a tuple $(X, \sigma_1, \sigma_2, \dots)$ where $X$ is a set (or class) and the $\sigma_i$ are operations, relations, or distinguished elements, subject to **axioms** expressed in first-order logic. A structure is **weaker** than another if it satisfies fewer axioms; the collection of structures of a given signature ordered this way forms a lattice. ::: The method of the whole subject: **start minimal, add one axiom at a time**, and watch the theory become richer. The diagrams below are the result. --- ## 2. The Algebraic Ladder ### 2.1 Magmas Through Groups | Structure | Signature | Axioms | Canonical example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Magma** (groupoid) | $({}\cdot{})$ | closure only | $(\mathbb{Z},-)$ | | **Semigroup** | $({}\cdot{})$ | associative | positive integers under $+$ | | **Monoid** | $({}\cdot{},e)$ | assoc. + identity | $(\mathbb{N},+,0)$ | | **Group** | $({}\cdot,{}^{-1},e)$ | monoid + inverses | $(\mathbb{Z},+)$, $S_n$ | | **Abelian group** | same | group + commutative | $(\mathbb{Z},+)$, $(\mathbb{Q},+)$ | | **Quasigroup** | $({}\cdot,/, \backslash)$ | division defined | loop theory | | **Loop** | quasigroup + $e$ | + identity | non-associative groups | Dropping commutativity of addition moves from abelian groups to general groups (e.g. the quaternion group $Q_8$, symmetric groups $S_n$ for $n\ge3$). ### 2.2 Rings Through Fields | Structure | Extra axiom | Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Ring (rng)** | two operations, distributive | $2\mathbb{Z}$ (no $1$) | | **Ring with unity** | multiplicative identity $1$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ | | **Commutative ring** | $ab=ba$ | $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ | | **Integral domain** | no zero divisors | $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ | | **UFD** | unique factorization into irreducibles | $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ | | **PID** | every ideal is principal | $\mathbb{Z}$, $k[x]$ | | **Euclidean domain** | division algorithm | $\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}[i]$ | | **Field** | every nonzero element invertible | $\mathbb{Q},\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C},\mathbb{F}_p$ | The chain is strict: $$ \text{fields} \subsetneq \text{Euclidean domains} \subsetneq \text{PIDs} \subsetneq \text{UFDs} \subsetneq \text{integral domains} \subsetneq \text{commutative rings}. $$ For example $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-5}]$ is an integral domain but not a UFD ($6=2\cdot3=(1+\sqrt{-5})(1-\sqrt{-5})$). ### 2.3 Modules, Vector Spaces, and Algebras - **Module over a ring $R$:** an abelian group $M$ with a scalar action $R\times M\to M$ satisfying the module axioms. $R=\mathbb{Z}$ recovers abelian groups; $R$ a field gives a **vector space**. - **Vector space over a field $k$:** a module over a field; every vector space has a **basis** (uses the Axiom of Choice in general), with a well-defined dimension. - **Algebra over a ring:** a ring that is also a module, with a compatible multiplication (e.g. matrix algebras, group algebras, Lie algebras). ### 2.4 Lattices and Boolean Algebras | Structure | Axioms | Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Partial order** | reflexive, antisym., transitive | $(\mathcal{P}(S),\subseteq)$ | | **Lattice** | every pair has meet $\wedge$ and join $\vee$ | divisors of $n$ under gcd/lcm | | **Distributive lattice** | $a\wedge(b\vee c)=(a\wedge b)\vee(a\wedge c)$ | Boolean algebras | | **Boolean algebra** | distributive + complements | $\mathcal{P}(S)$ with $\cap,\cup,{}^c$ | | **Heyting algebra** | distributive + relative pseudo-complement | open sets of a topology | Boolean algebras model propositional logic and digital circuits; Heyting algebras model **intuitionistic** logic (dropping the law of excluded middle — connecting to the [constructivist discussion](uncountable-infinities-diagonal-argument-and-cantor-set-fractals.qmd)). --- ## 3. Categories, Functors, and Monads ::: {#def-category} #### Definition 3.1 (Category) A **category** $\mathcal{C}$ consists of objects $\operatorname{ob}\mathcal{C}$, morphisms $\hom(A,B)$ for each pair, a composition $\circ:\hom(B,C)\times\hom(A,B)\to\hom(A,C)$, and identity morphisms $\mathrm{id}_A$, satisfying: $$ (h\circ g)\circ f=h\circ(g\circ f),\qquad \mathrm{id}_B\circ f=f=f\circ \mathrm{id}_A. $$ ::: - A **monoid is exactly a one-object category** (elements = morphisms, $e=\mathrm{id}$). - A **groupoid** is a category in which every morphism is invertible (a group is a one-object groupoid). - A **functor** preserves objects, morphisms, identities, and composition. - A **natural transformation** compares functors. - A **monad** is an endofunctor $T$ with natural transformations $\eta:\mathrm{Id}\to T$ (**unit**) and $\mu:T^2\to T$ (**join**) satisfying the monad laws ($\mu\circ T\mu=\mu\circ\mu T$, $\mu\circ \eta T=\mathrm{id}=\mu\circ T\eta$). Monads are the categorical theory of **effects** (nondeterminism, state, exceptions, IO), central to functional programming (Haskell) and to algebraic theories (Eilenberg–Moore algebras). This is the precise sense in which the user's chain "magmas … monads" lives on **two axes at once**: algebraic (groups, rings, fields) and categorical (monoid = one-object category; monad = monoid in the category of endofunctors). --- ## 4. The Spatial Ladder ::: {#def-spaces} #### Ladders of Spaces $$ \begin{aligned} &\textbf{Set} \to \textbf{Topological space} \to \textbf{Metric space} \to \textbf{Normed space} \to \textbf{Inner product space} \to \textbf{Hilbert space},\\ &\textbf{Metric space} \to \textbf{Uniform space} \to \textbf{Topological space} \quad(\text{reversed}),\\ &\textbf{Measurable space} \to \textbf{Measure space} \to \textbf{Probability space},\\ &\textbf{Topological manifold} \to \textbf{Smooth manifold} \to \textbf{Riemannian manifold} \to \textbf{Lorentzian manifold}. \end{aligned} $$ ::: | Space | Added structure | Key theorem | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Set** | none | cardinality | | **Topological space** | open sets | continuity, compactness, connectedness | | **Metric space** | distance | completion, Baire, Heine–Borel | | **Normed space** | norm $\lVert x\rVert$ | triangle inequality, metric from norm | | **Inner product space** | $\langle x,y\rangle$ | Cauchy–Schwarz, orthogonality, projections | | **Hilbert space** | complete inner product | Riesz representation, spectral theorem | | **Banach space** | complete normed | Banach fixed point, open mapping | | **Measurable space** | $\sigma$-algebra | measurability | | **Measure space** | measure $\mu$ | Lebesgue integration, monotone/Fatou/dominated convergence | | **Probability space** | measure with $\mu(\Omega)=1$ | LLN, CLT | | **Manifold** | locally Euclidean topology | charts, tangent spaces, Stokes' theorem | Every normed space is metric ($d(x,y)=\lVert x-y\rVert$); every inner product space is normed ($\lVert x\rVert=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle}$); every metric space is topological (open balls); not conversely — the cofinite topology is non-metrizable, and $\ell^p$ for $0set + binary op"] --> SG["Semigroup

The green node is the algebraic summit (fields); the blue node is the analytic summit (Hilbert spaces); the orange node is the categorical summit (monads); the red node is the physics workhorse (C*-algebras). The hybrid subgraph shows where different ladders **meet**. --- ## 7. Why Each Axiom Matters (Counterexamples) | Weaker structure | What fails | Witness | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Magma not semigroup | associativity | $(\mathbb{Z},-)$ | | Semigroup not monoid | identity | $(\{1,2,3,\dots\},+)$ | | Monoid not group | inverses | $(\mathbb{N},+,0)$ | | Group not abelian | commutativity | $S_3$, $Q_8$ | | Ring not commutative | $ab=ba$ | matrix ring $M_2(\mathbb{R})$ | | Commutative ring not domain | zero divisors | $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ | | Domain not UFD | unique factorization | $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{-5}]$ | | UFD not PID | principal ideals | $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ | | PID not Euclidean | division algorithm | some $O_K$ | | Topological not metric | distance | cofinite topology | | Metric not normed | homogeneity of norm | $\ell^p$, $0 not a group)") print("\n=== 3. RING vs FIELD: Z_n UNDER + AND × ===") def is_field(n): if n < 2: return False S = list(range(n)) add_closed = all((a+b) % n in S for a in S for b in S) mul_assoc = all((a*b)*c % n == a*(b*c) % n for a in S for b in S for c in S) distrib = all(a*(b+c) % n == (a*b + a*c) % n for a in S for b in S for c in S) inv = all(any((a*b) % n == 1 for b in S) for a in S if a != 0) return add_closed and mul_assoc and distrib and inv for n in [4, 5, 6, 7, 11]: print(f" Z_{n} is a field: {is_field(n)} (prime => True)") print("\n=== 4. VECTOR SPACE AXIOMS IN R^2 ===") import random random.seed(0) def add(u, v): return (u[0]+v[0], u[1]+v[1]) def smul(c, u): return (c*u[0], c*u[1]) vecs = [(random.randint(-9, 9), random.randint(-9, 9)) for _ in range(50)] scalars = [random.randint(-5, 5) for _ in range(20)] # integers => exact arithmetic assoc_add = all(add(add(u,v),w) == add(u,add(v,w)) for u in vecs for v in vecs for w in vecs) comm_add = all(add(u,v) == add(v,u) for u in vecs for v in vecs) zero = (0,0) ident = all(add(u, zero) == u for u in vecs) distrib1 = all(smul(c, add(u,v)) == add(smul(c,u), smul(c,v)) for c in scalars for u in vecs for v in vecs) distrib2 = all(smul(c+d, u) == add(smul(c,u), smul(d,u)) for c in scalars for d in scalars for u in vecs) print(f" associativity={assoc_add}, commutativity={comm_add}, zero={ident}, distributivity={distrib1 and distrib2}") print("\n=== 5. LATTICE: DIVISORS OF 12 UNDER gcd/lcm ===") from math import gcd def lcm(a, b): return a*b // gcd(a, b) divs = [d for d in range(1, 13) if 12 % d == 0] meet_join = all(gcd(a,b) in divs and lcm(a,b) in divs for a in divs for b in divs) distrib = all(gcd(a, lcm(b,c)) == lcm(gcd(a,b), gcd(a,c)) for a in divs for b in divs for c in divs) print(f" divisors={divs}; closed under meet/join={meet_join}; distributive={distrib}") print("\n=== 6. BOOLEAN ALGEBRA: POWER SET OF {1,2,3} ===") U = {1,2,3} Power = [frozenset(s) for r in range(4) for s in itertools.combinations(U, r)] def comp(A): return frozenset(U - A) distrib = all((A & (B | C)) == ((A & B) | (A & C)) for A in Power for B in Power for C in Power) complement = all((A | comp(A)) == frozenset(U) and (A & comp(A)) == frozenset() for A in Power) print(f" |P(U)|={len(Power)}; distributive={distrib}; complements={complement}") print("\n=== 7. SMALL CATEGORY: IDENTITY AND ASSOCIATIVITY ===") # Objects A, B; morphisms idA, idB, f: A -> B. Represent a morphism by (domain, codomain). morph = {'idA': ('A', 'A'), 'idB': ('B', 'B'), 'f': ('A', 'B')} def compose(g, h): """Return g ∘ h (apply h first): h: X->Y, g: Y->Z.""" if h[1] != g[0]: return None if h in (morph['idA'], morph['idB']): return g if g in (morph['idA'], morph['idB']): return h return (h[0], g[1]) ids_ok = True for name, (X, Y) in morph.items(): idX = ('A', 'A') if X == 'A' else ('B', 'B') idY = ('A', 'A') if Y == 'A' else ('B', 'B') left = compose(idY, morph[name]) # id_Y ∘ m right = compose(morph[name], idX) # m ∘ id_X print(f" {name} ({X}->{Y}): id_Y∘{name}={left}, {name}∘id_X={right}") if left != morph[name] or right != morph[name]: ids_ok = False print(f" identity laws hold: {ids_ok}") print(f" composition f ∘ idA = {compose(morph['f'], morph['idA'])}") print("\n=== 8. THE LIST MONAD: UNIT AND BIND LAWS ===") unit = lambda x: [x] def bind(xs, f): return [y for x in xs for y in f(x)] f = lambda x: [x, x+1] g = lambda x: [x*10] m = [1, 2, 3] left_id = bind(unit(7), f) == f(7) right_id = bind(m, unit) == m assoc = bind(bind(m, f), g) == bind(m, lambda x: bind(f(x), g)) print(f" left identity (unit a >>= f = f a): {left_id}") print(f" right identity (m >>= unit = m): {right_id}") print(f" associativity (m >>= f) >>= g: {assoc}") print(" => List is a monad: the categorical structure behind nondeterminism.") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` === 1. FINITE GROUP: (Z_n, +) AND (Z_p*, ×) === (Z_4, +): closed=(True, True, True, True) (Z_5, +): closed=(True, True, True, True) (Z_6, +): closed=(True, True, True, True) (Z_p*, ×) is a group iff p prime: p=5: (True, True, True, True) (field iff all inverses) p=6: (False, True, True, False) (field iff all inverses) p=7: (True, True, True, True) (field iff all inverses) === 2. THE LIST MONAD: UNIT AND BIND LAWS === left identity (unit a >>= f = f a): True right identity (m >>= unit = m): True associativity (m >>= f) >>= g: True => List is a monad: the categorical structure behind nondeterminism. ``` ::: ::: --- ## 9. Summary $$ \begin{aligned} &\textbf{Algebra: } && \text{magma}\to\text{semigroup}\to\text{monoid}\to\text{group}\to\text{ring}\to\text{field};\\ & && \text{module}\to\text{vector space};\ \text{partial order}\to\text{lattice}\to\text{Boolean algebra}.\\[3pt] &\textbf{Categories: } && \text{monoid}=\text{one-object category};\ \text{group}=\text{one-object groupoid};\ \text{monad}=\text{monoid of endofunctors}.\\[3pt] &\textbf{Spaces: } && \text{Set}\to\text{Top}\to\text{Metric}\to\text{Normed}\to\text{Inner}\to\text{Hilbert};\ \ \text{Measure}\to\text{Probability}.\\[3pt] &\textbf{Hybrids: } && \text{topological/Lie groups, Banach/C*-algebras, Riemannian manifolds.} \end{aligned} $$ The hierarchy is the periodic table of mathematics: each structure is a setting in which certain theorems become true, and the functors between them translate results from one setting to another. --- ## 10.
